column_notes.name, url, language, stars, forks, last_: copied from seed_v2.csv, repeated on every row of the repo
column_notes.scan_status: scanned | no_packages (report with 0 packages) | not_scanned (no report yet) | report_error (report unreadable; reason in report_warning)
column_notes.report_source: json, csv (the .json was missing or unreadable) or none
column_notes.report_file: report file name in reports/ (sbom.generate_safe_filename of the url)
column_notes.report_timestamp: when the report was written (scan time)
column_notes.report_total_packages: packages in the report (summary.total_packages for json)
column_notes.report_total_vulnerabilities: Grype matches in the report (json summary; empty for csv)
column_notes.report_warning: ';'-joined: count_mismatch (summary.total_packages differs from the package list), target_mismatch (report target is not the seed url), from_csv, duplicates_dropped=N, or the read error
column_notes.package_name, package_version, package_t: report 'package', 'version', 'type' (Syft type: npm, python, github-action, ...). Versions are as sbom.py stores them: a leading 'v' removed; missing or a 40-character commit hash -> 'unknown'
column_notes.ecosystem: the database rule of sbom.py: python/pypi -> python, npm/node -> npm, anything else -> none (never looked up)
column_notes.report_latest_version, report_version_st: report 'latest_version' and 'version_status' as looked up at report_timestamp. When the lookup failed or the type is not looked up, the report copies the installed version, so the status is up_to_date; use the database / daily snapshots for registry data
column_notes.vulnerability_id: the first Grype match only, or 'None'
column_notes.severity: the highest severity among the package's matches, or 'None'
column_notes.fixed_version: report placeholder ('See advisory' or 'N/A'), not a real version
column_notes.db_row: kept = the row the database stores (one versions row per package name per repo, names compared case-insensitively, the last occurrence wins); collapsed = an earlier row with the same name

rules: One row per (repo, package). A repo without packages (not_scanned, no_packages, report_error) has one row with the package columns empty.
Packages are unique per (name, version, type) within a repo; exact duplicates are dropped and counted (report_warning duplicates_dropped=N).

sbom.py already merges packages by name:version before writing the report, so the counts are its de-duplicated counts, not raw Syft artifact counts (dataset/pilot_syft_results.csv). Raw Syft output is not saved.
The database keeps fewer rows: one per package name per repo. Filter db_row = kept to get the database's row set.
Latest version, version status and vulnerability fields are scan-time values from the report; see the column notes for their limits.
Built from files only: no MySQL and no network. Rows follow seed_v2.csv order, then report package order.
